localChanges: The six layers that draw a tile's own scenery — land and coast, irrigation, terrain, improvements, terrain features and goody huts — were six world-sized canvases the portal composited in order on every render. Nothing ever toggled any of them on its own and they only change when a tile changes, so they are one `Landscape` canvas now, drawn in the same order. The main portal holds seven world canvases instead of twelve, and the city portal six instead of ten; the city map gains goody huts, which it had been the only portal not to draw.

`Portal.render()` drew every layer at every wrapped offset as a full-layer blit, including offsets that fell entirely off the canvas. It works out once, for all the layers, which repeats land on the canvas and which part of each one does. On an 80x60 world at scale 2 in a 1712x873 portal that takes a render from 60.5 `drawImage` calls and 297 megapixels of source down to 15.0 calls and 7.5 megapixels.
The marker for a road with no neighbouring road called `rect()` and `fill()` without a `beginPath()`, so every marker re-filled every isolated road drawn before it. It begins a path now.
